channel.title: Legacy Medical Journal
channel.description: Health notes from Legacy Medical, a concierge internal medicine practice in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida.

item.title: Vitamins that can be taken in the morning
item.description: Vitamin B12, vitamin C, iron, magnesium and zinc are often taken in the morning. A short guide to why, and which other supplements are used for energy.

item.title: Breast cancer screening update
item.description: The USPSTF's 2024 update moved routine mammograms for average-risk women to every other year from age 40 to 74, and how the ACR and ACS differ.

item.title: Magnesium: a forgotten electrolyte
item.description: Why magnesium runs low (diet, diarrhea, acid reducers, diuretics) or high in kidney disease, the symptoms of each, and why to check before supplementing.

item.title: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents: hidden dangers in the pharmacy aisle
item.description: Ibuprofen and naproxen are sold without a prescription, but NSAIDs can harm the kidneys, stomach, heart and blood. Why they are meant for short-term use.

item.title: RSV infection in adults
item.description: How RSV spreads, which adults are at highest risk of severe illness, how long people stay contagious, and the everyday steps that help prevent infection.

item.title: Benefits of yearly influenza vaccination
item.description: Why a yearly flu shot matters, who is at higher risk of flu complications, who should not get the vaccine, and when in the season to be vaccinated.

item.title: How often should someone urinate?
item.description: Most adults urinate about 6 to 8 times a day. Common reasons for urinating more or less often, from fluids and medications to prostate and kidney problems.

item.title: What is low-dose computed tomography?
item.description: Low-dose CT is a yearly lung cancer screening test. Who is eligible under USPSTF criteria, what a pack-year is, the risks of screening, and when to stop.

item.title: The benefits of exercising
item.description: Regular exercise lowers the risk of heart disease, diabetes, some cancers and falls, and helps mood, sleep, bones and weight. Check with your doctor first.

item.title: Potty like a rockstar: constipation and the squatty potty
item.description: What counts as constipation, which symptoms need urgent care, first steps with fiber, fluids and exercise, and how a toilet stool straightens the colon.

item.title: What is a pulse oximeter?
item.description: How a fingertip pulse oximeter measures blood oxygen, how to take an accurate reading at home, what the numbers mean, and what can throw readings off.

item.title: Safety of over-the-counter oral pain medications
item.description: Acetaminophen and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen and naproxen carry FDA boxed warnings. The liver, heart, stomach and kidney risks to know before you take them.

item.title: CDC COVID-19 booster update
item.description: The CDC's November 2021 COVID-19 booster guidance for Pfizer, Moderna and Johnson & Johnson recipients, kept as a record. Current guidance is different.

item.title: Bananas are an amazing source of nutrition
item.description: What a banana gives you: potassium, magnesium, fiber and resistant starch, plus why people with kidney disease or diabetes may need to limit them.

item.title: Let's talk about antibiotics: the good, the bad and the ugly
item.description: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not viral ones. The side effects of using them when they are not needed, and how overuse leads to resistance.

item.title: Vitamin supplementation
item.description: How the FDA regulates dietary supplements, who may benefit from a multivitamin, and the risks of taking too much vitamin A, beta-carotene or vitamin D.

item.title: The Mediterranean diet approach
item.description: What the Mediterranean diet emphasizes, why olive oil, nuts and fish matter for the heart, how wine fits in, and practical steps to start eating this way.

item.title: Is cancer preventable?
item.description: Tobacco, infections, alcohol, obesity, air pollution, sun exposure and diet: the cancers linked to each risk factor and the prevention steps for each one.

item.title: Fully vaccinated? Now what?
item.description: A short 2021 note for patients newly vaccinated against COVID-19: keep testing if you have symptoms and follow CDC and health department travel advice.

item.title: Why is obesity a disease?
item.description: Why the American Medical Association has recognized obesity as a disease since 2013, how hunger signals are affected, and what modest weight loss can do.
